subject: Private deployment SLA — infrastructure responsibility exclusion request (Velaris Labs)
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@velaris.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Lim <sara.lim@velaris.ai>
Date: Tue, 08 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment SLA — infra carveout question

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Velaris is preparing a Private deployment for our inference traffic (on-prem cluster behind our firewall) and our legal team has flagged a section in the draft SLA that references "Redwood-managed infrastructure availability".

Given that the compute, networking, and storage will be controlled by Velaris (we will manage rack-level maintenance, network peering, and host-level OS updates), the legal team is asking whether Redwood is willing to accept an explicit exclusion for customer-controlled infrastructure availability and network tail latency in the Private deployment SLA. Specifically:

- Exclude customer network outages and third-party datacenter incidents from Redwood's uptime/latency commitments.
- Provide an agreed shared-responsibility table with clear operational boundaries and example failure modes.

We can share our network topology and a list of maintenance windows. Happy to send the security pack and SOC2 snapshot; I attached an initial bundle.

Can you confirm whether Redwood has a standard carveout clause for Private/VPC/on-prem deployments, or if you prefer to discuss language we propose?

Regards,
Alex

--
Alex Chen
Head of Platform Engineering, Velaris Labs
alex.chen@velaris.ai
Attachment: velaris-soc2-snapshot-2028-04.zip (zip)
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@velaris.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 09 May 2028 10:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment SLA — infra carveout question

Hi Alex —

Appreciate the clear summary and the SOC2 bundle. Short answer: yes, Redwood treats Private/VPC/on-prem customer-controlled infra differently from Hosted service SLAs. We can include carveouts for customer-managed network and host-level incidents, but we try to keep them narrow and prescriptive so there isn’t an open-ended removal of recovery obligations.

What I propose as next steps:

1) Vivek (cc'd) will propose a compact shared-responsibility table that maps incident types to owners and gives example mitigations.
2) Rishi (cc'd) will coordinate with Legal on minimal carveout language and any fallback expectations (e.g., if KV cache loss occurs because of host reboot, what retries/fallbacks Redwood will provide).
3) Monica/Rishi — we will review the example maintenance windows and network topology you sent, Alex. If Velaris has scheduled host reboots during batched inference windows, we will call those out as operational constraints.

I attached a short draft with preferred carveout phrasing (PDF) — it's intentionally conservative. If Velaris prefers more permissive language, we can iterate. Also flagging that a small SLA fee adjustment may apply when we accept broader exclusions; our Commercial team will surface that in a redline.

Can we set a 30-minute sync on Friday to walk the table and redline?

Thanks,
Monica

--
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai
Attachment: velaris-sla-redlines.pdf (pdf)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@velaris.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 May 2028 14:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment SLA — infra carveout question

Alex / Monica —

Following up with a draft shared-responsibility matrix below (high level). This is intended as the starting point for the SLA amendment. Happy to expand examples into an appendix if Legal wants more forensic scenarios.

- Customer network outages (e.g., BGP flap, datacenter power failure): Customer responsibility. Redwood will provide degraded-mode guidance and recommend regional fallback if available; SLA credits not applicable.
- Host OS/kernel/driver issues on customer-managed hosts: Customer responsibility. If guest-level degradation occurs that we can mitigate via retry/backoff at the runtime layer, Redwood will attempt mitigation but will not be liable for uptime credits.
- Redwood service software failures (model runtime, kernel selection bugs, cache corruption originating in Redwood code): Redwood responsibility — standard SLA applies.
- Third-party storage/service degradation (customer-managed): Customer responsibility unless Redwood operates a directly connected service under contract.

Operational notes:
- We request a 2-hour scheduled maintenance window for host-level updates. For unscheduled host reboot events (e.g., kernel panic), we ask Velaris to surface node-level logs within 48 hours to aid root-cause analysis; the absence of logs may limit remediation scope.
- For latency SLAs, we propose excluding "customer network tail latency" (last-mile and customer peering) and tying Redwood latency commitments to the time-to-first-byte from our runtime to the customer gateway.

I'll put these points into the formal amendment draft and send to Rishi to fold into the SLA redline. Markus — can you confirm whether a nominal SLA fee uplift (we suggested +5% to baseline for broader exclusions) is acceptable to Commercial for this account?

Vivek

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Product Operations, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@velaris.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Lim <sara.lim@velaris.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 16:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment SLA — infra carveout question

Thanks — that draft matrix looks reasonable and pragmatic. A few quick replies:

- Velaris accepts the high-level split you propose. We will prepare the node logs and agree to the 48-hour window for sharing diagnostic artifacts.
- For the latency carveout, can we surface a short definition we can include in the SLA: "Customer network tail latency = packet delay attributable to customer-managed WAN/peering and last-mile infrastructure." That will help avoid disputes.
- On the fee uplift — please send the Commercial note and we can route it through Procurement.

We'll take the redline when it lands and respond. Friday 10:30am PT would work for a 30-minute sync; I can send a calendar invite after you confirm.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Alex

--
Alex Chen
Head of Platform Engineering, Velaris Labs
alex.chen@velaris.ai
